knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Section 6.1 and the regulations: total chlorine above 10 mg/L means a public pool or spa has to be shut to bathers at once.
Section 2 Definitions and section 6.1: free chlorine is the uncombined portion that kills organisms and destroys pollutants.
Table 1: unstabilised pools at more than 26 degrees need at least 2.0 mg/L free chlorine; 1.0 mg/L applies at 26 degrees or cooler.

practicalCriteria: On a supplied pool, measures free and total chlorine and temperature, and states whether each reading is in range.
Given a total chlorine reading above 10 mg/L in a scenario, closes the pool, notifies the operator and records the time without delay.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Chlorine test record for the assessed pool
Closure record in a supplied scenario
stopWorkCriteria: Total chlorine above 10 mg/L: close the pool, do not dose further, and escalate.
Chlorine gas smell in an enclosure: leave, raise the alarm, follow the site emergency procedure.
Free chlorine below minimum: keep the pool closed until a passing retest is recorded.
